authorship: Numerical check of Gemini hypotheses supplied by Kyle; not an inferred orbit or physical fit.
assumptions: Circular relative orbit; Kepler a^3=Mtotal P^2 in AU, solar masses, years. Uniform blackbody grains in radiative equilibrium; L=55 Lsun illustrative, not an accepted atmospheric solution.
qualifications: Two separated dimming episodes do not establish an 88-year recurrence period or prove they share a mechanism.
Transverse path length is v*t for a central edge-on circular crossing, not a unique disk diameter; impact parameter, inclination, opacity gradients and eccentricity matter.
Disk stability, companion mass and precession timescale require an explicit dynamical model. A close binary alone does not imply a dusty torus.
Infrared luminosity depends on total intercepted starlight and dust temperature, grain properties and geometry; line-of-sight depth is not bolometric covering fraction.
No warm excess does not establish a cold distant disk; a warm excess does not uniquely establish a circumbinary ring.
